description.narrative: The project is investing in rehabilitation and expansion of sewerage network, modernization and expansion of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), and improvement of wastewater management in the Kathmandu Valley that will help improve service delivery and reduce pollution of the Bagmati River and its tributaries. The project is also strengthening the institutions working for wastewater management in the Kathmandu Valley to increase operational efficiency and improve service delivery, and will result in positive impacts on health and quality of life for the residents of Kathmandu Valley. The project is coordinating with other related projects to fulfill the medium-term priority investment needs identified in the long-term capital investment and asset management program.

description.narrative: Improved access to, and efficiency of, wastewater services for the residents of Kathmandu Valley.

New sewer connections provided to 58,850 buildings (168,900 households) (Target: 30% of new beneficiaries are from poor households; 100% of households in the service area headed by women are benefitted). Progress/Status: No activities at Output level transpiring household sewer connection at Outcome level is envisaged/or in the scope of the project. Data Source: - Quarterly Progress reports & Annual reports - ADB Review Mission aide-memoires - Contract completion reports Actual value:

Wastewater treatment capacity increased from 16.4 MLD in 2012 to 90.5 MLD in 2018. Achievement: 32.4 Progress/Status: WW/TP/01, WW/TP/02 and WW/TP/03 are under implementation for rehabilitation, expansion and construction of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) for a total capacity of 138.1 MLD. One treatment plant (TP-01) of 32.4 MLD capacity at Guheshwori completed and is in operation; TP-03 in Dhobighat (37 MLD) was in trial run stage but September 2024 flood disrupted. 2nd (of 4 stages) testing is ongoing; TP-02 reprocured (contract awarded on 12 June 2024) after termination of the earlier contract and contractor is mobilized, and contractor is performing the civil works of WWTPs different components but at a slow pace.
Two new decentralized treatment facilities of capacity 3 MLD and 1 MLD at Gokarna and Hanumanghat, respectively under contract package KUKL/DEWATS are under implementation. The implementation had been severely delayed and started improving lately.
Thus, total capacity will increase to 142.1 MLD after completion of all WWTPs and DEWATS. Data Source: - Quarterly Progress reports & Annual reports - ADB Review Mission aide-memoires - Contract completion reports

By the end of the project (by 2018) Collection of sewage through sewerage network increased from less than 5% in 2012 to more than 80% in 2018. Progress/Status: Three interceptor sewer packages under implementation and substantially completed with descoping of some portion in 2 packages ensuring the designed collection of sewage discharge. Collection coverage to be assessed at project completion. Data Source: - Quarterly Progress reports & Annual reports - ADB Review Mission aide-memoires - Contract completion reports Actual value:

Samples of effluent from wastewater treatment plants complying with national effluent standards increased from less than 5% in 2012 to almost 100% in 2018. Progress/Status: Likely to be achieved by project end. Completed Guheshwori WWTP effluent generally meets KPI however a third party monitoring has shown varying results. Output: 2. Wastewater treatment plants modernized and expanded. Indicator: By the end of the project (by 2021) Five WWTPs rehabilitated. Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Five WWTPs under construction with a total capacity of 138.1 MLD:
i.) WW/TP/01 - Guheshwori (32.4 MLD: construction completed and the plant is under O&M phase. However, O&M of the plant is not satisfactory.
ii.) WW/TP/02 - Sallaghari, Kodku and Dhobighat (68.7 MLD): Contract terminated in September 2022 after achievement of 26.47% of overall contract scope. New contract was mobilized since 26 June 2024 and works ongoing of the three WWTPs but at slow pace. The overall progress of the contract is 60.94% against the elapsed time of 76% (without 5 years O&M period). Progress of the each plants is below: • Sallaghari: 58% against elapsed time of 91%. • Kodku: 67% against elapsed time of 91%. • Dhobighat WWTP: 57% against elapsed time of 76%.
iii.) WW/TP/03 - Dhobighat (37 MLD): Overall Progress: All civil works and hydromechanical installations completed with overall physical progress of 97% against the elapsed time of 97%. The plant was ready for three months testing and trial run stage but the plant suffered major damages to the late September 2025 flooding bringing complete halt of the trial run. Damage assessment for insurance claim is completed, and the contractor has resumed the testing and commissioning of the WWTP with Stage-2 tests ongoing.
Data Source: - Project progress reports, quarterly reports, annual reports - ADB Review Mission aide-memoires.
